title: True speech: person begets person in unity of essence — Cap. 22 COMPLETE
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): CHAPTER TWENTY-THREE, On ye SON, follows. person a person, hypostasis a hypostasis, not out from essence but in ye unity belonging toward essence, that same which ye Father gave wholly to ye Son, not by means belonging toward alienation but by means belonging toward communication — but truly plus properly it stands as said that same ye Father has begotten ye Son. God out from His essence begets God. essence begets a person; the divine essence begets or stands as begotten; such as: — therefore those who love to speak cautiously plus circumspectly avoid certain belonging toward ye ancients kyriologies. impious, even sacrilegious — therefore to reduce ye mode belonging toward this generation to ye laws belonging toward human nativity or belonging toward any created thing stands as inept. as genera plus species stand as conceived in our intellects operation, but even when our intellects operation ceases, there stands as a true multiplication belonging toward hypostases, plus a true distinction belonging toward them, without any confusion or separation among themselves — yet this secret stands as not placed in speculation alone.
pass_b_english: Yet this secret is not placed in speculation alone, as genera and species are conceived in our intellects operation, but even when our intellects operation ceases, there is a true multiplication of hypostases, and a true distinction of them, without any confusion or separation among themselves.

Therefore to reduce the mode of this generation to the laws of human nativity or of any created thing is inept, impious, even sacrilegious. Therefore those who love to speak cautiously and circumspectly avoid certain of the ancients kyriologies, such as: the divine essence begets or is begotten; essence begets a person; God from His essence begets God.

But truly and properly it is said that the Father has begotten the Son, person a person, hypostasis a hypostasis, not from essence but in the unity of essence, which the Father gave wholly to the Son, not by alienation but by communication. CHAPTER TWENTY-THREE, On the SON, follows.
source_text: Neque tamen hoc arcanum in sola speculatione positum est, sicuti in intellectus nostri operatione genera et species concipiuntur, sed cessante etiam intellectus nostri operatione, vera est hypostaseon multiplicatio, veraque earum distinctio, citra ullam inter se confusionem aut separationem. Hujus igitur generationis modum ad humanae nativitatis aut ullius creatae rei leges revocare, ineptum, impium, imo sacrilegum est. Quapropter, qui caute et circumspecte loqui amant, quasdam veterum kyriologias vitant, quales sunt: divinam essentiam gignere vel gigni; essentiam gignere personam; Deum ex sua essentia gignere Deum. Vere autem et proprie dicitur, Patrem genuisse Filium, personam personam, hypostasin hypostasin, non ex essentia, sed in unitate essentiae, quam Pater Filio totam dedit, non alienatione, sed communicatione. CAPUT VIGESIMUM TERTIUM, De FILIO, sequitur.
